summary: New `remote` Cargo feature, off by default. lib.rs compiles `remote` and `host_pair` only with it; rcgen and qrcode become optional deps enabled by it; rustls drops its `tls12` feature (zenpi's TLS listener is 1.3-only; ureq still enables tls12 for provider HTTPS). Without the feature: `zenpi host pair|serve` is refused with an explicit error and left out of --help; RemoteApprovalActor, AcceptedApproval.remote and respond_remote are compiled out (respond_fenced now takes an attribution closure); every wakeup::notify call (approval, session, project_workspace, tui PTY) is cfg-gated; the remote receipt/ack/intent types, the remote pool fields and ~30 remote-only ProjectOwnerPool methods are gated, and the default build never reads remote-state.json except to move a legacy inline copy out unchanged; worktree::{worker, worker_admission, worker_progress, worktree_runner, worktree_host} and subtab::{listing, mutate} are remote-only (only remote requests create worker owners), subtab state stays in the core build; the TUI desktop remote host, pairing overlay, remote prompt progress and desktop text preview are gated. valid_identifier moves to crate::protocol (re-exported by remote::auth). Remote test suites carry #![cfg(feature = "remote")] (remote_auth, which remote_security include!s, uses required-features in Cargo.toml); the Android interop script runs with --features remote. bench_runtime counts only non-optional direct deps, tightens normal_dependencies_max 21 -> 19 and adds a core_dependency_boundary gate (no tokio, rcgen or qrcode in the default tree).

notes: Deviations: (1) The default release artifact (tools/release.sh, cargo install) no longer contains the Android remote host; pairing needs `--features remote`. (2) Besides the files owned by ZE-520, gating touched src/headless.rs (ProcessResult field initialisers), src/protocol.rs (valid_identifier), src/remote/auth.rs (re-export), src/worktree/{mod,subtab,worker}.rs, src/project_workspace.rs, tools/build_android_interop_classes.sh, .github/workflows/ci.yml and test files; tests that assert remote wakeups or remote approval attribution are gated, and tests/tui_task.rs's source-shape assertion follows the new run_tui_loop call. (3) Without remote the restore path no longer imports journal admissions, so it opens each saved journal explicitly to keep refusing a checkpoint that names an unreadable journal. (4) ring and rustls stay direct non-optional dependencies (ureq pulls both; backend explicit TLS tests use rustls). The single `let _ = session;` in ApprovalCoordinator::bind_notification_session keeps the non-remote signature without an allow attribute. CI: the main test step already runs --all-features (which includes remote); the Android interop step now runs its suites with --features remote. The checkpoint written by a remote build is loaded by the default build: tests/headless_project_workspace.rs project_checkpoint_restores_beside_remote_state_and_moves_legacy_inline_state_out passes in both builds (remote-state.json beside the checkpoint is left untouched; a legacy inline copy is moved out byte-for-byte equivalent). No new unwrap/expect/panic in non-test code; no new unsafe. Rebased onto origin/main 2e483b1 (ZE-400..404 landed during the work); ZE-510 and ZE-511 applied cleanly.
